summary:
BIO-SHIELD 3D is an autonomous, real-time astronaut health monitoring and clinical decision-support software engineered for long-duration space missions without onboard physicians. Built with a Python/Flask backend, SQL database persistence, and an interactive Three.js 3D holographic interface, the platform continuously tracks vital signs (heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure/MAP, Shock Index, glucose, sleep, and bone density) alongside CSA radiation dosimetry, webcam fatigue detection, and simulated POCUS ultrasound diagnostics.

It directly addresses the Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions challenge by solving deep-space communication delays (up to 16+ minutes to Earth) and modeling NASA’s five human spaceflight hazards (RIDGE) against real NASA OSDR baselines. When a critical anomaly strikes, the software automatically highlights the affected anatomical zone on a personalized 3D avatar and triggers a hands-free, voice-guided, step-by-step emergency triage protocol with an acoustic CPR metronome.

This software is vital because deep-space survival demands empowering non-medical crew members to act decisively—while offering immediate dual-use value for isolated rural clinics on Earth.
